issue.title: Bug: Control plane fails to use backup route when connected route link goes down

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

In the data path, when a link goes down, any directly connected routes are removed, allowing the system to switch to alternative BGP-learned routes. However, in the control plane (kernel), connected routes remain active even when the link is down, leading to traffic failures.

### Steps to Reproduce

Have configuration to have two routes to same destination and shutdown the link with direct connect route.

```bash
root@sonic:/home/admin# ip route
default via <IP> dev eth0
<IP>/30 dev Ethernet0 proto kernel scope link src <IP>
**<IP>/30 dev PortChannel02 scope link linkdown**                               <-- Connected route
**<IP>/30 via <IP> dev Ethernet0 proto bgp src <IP> metric 20**     <-- BGP learnt route
<IP>/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src <IP>
<IP> via <IP> dev Ethernet0 proto bgp src <IP> metric 20
<IP>/24 dev docker0 proto kernel scope link src <IP> linkdown
```

```bash
#show ip route
Codes: K - kernel route, C - connected, S - static, R - RIP,
       O - OSPF, I - IS-IS, B - BGP, E - EIGRP, N - NHRP,
       T - Table, v - VNC, V - VNC-Direct, A - Babel, D - SHARP,
       F - PBR, f - OpenFabric,
       > - selected route, * - FIB route, q - queued route, r - rejected route
K>*<IP>/0 [0/0] via <IP>, eth0, <IPV6>
C>*<IP>/30 is directly connected, Ethernet0, <IPV6>
B>*<IP>/30 [200/0] via <IP>, Ethernet0, <IPV6>                    <-- BGP learnt route
C>*<IP>/24 is directly connected, eth0, <IPV6>
K <IP>/24 [0/0] is directly connected, eth0, <IPV6>
C>*<IP>/32 is directly connected, Loopback0, <IPV6>
B>*<IP>/32 [200/0] via <IP>, Ethernet0, <IPV6>
K <IP>/24 [0/0] is directly connected, docker0, inactive <IPV6>
```

Ping an IP in the subnet
```bash
# ping <IP>
PING <IP> (<IP>) 56(84) bytes of data.
^C
--- <IP> ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 2044ms
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Control path and data path behavior must be the same. Kernel should also skip using
connected routes whose link is down

resolution.title: sysctl: enable ignore_routes_with_linkdown for IPv4 and IPv6
resolution.description:
Fixes #24462

Today in Sonic, control path continues to use connected routes even when the link is down, despite alternative routes being available, causing traffic failure. This behavior differs from data path, which removes the downed connected route and switches to alternatives.

Enabling ignore_routes_with_linkdown sysctl aligns control and data path behavior by allowing control path to fallback to BGP-learned routes with lower metrics.

Once the link is restored, the connected route is reused.

This behavior follows FRR documentation and standard Linux network manager practices.

#### Why I did it
To avoid control path traffic failure and have common behavior across control and data path

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
Enabled ignore_routes_with_linkdown sysctl parameter
